# Lenz 0.0.19 beta

Lenz Code now asks before it runs anything that comes from a folder itself (PR #57). Updating is recommended.

- A folder you have not trusted opens in **Restricted** mode. Language servers and formatters that run code from the project stay off: rust-analyzer, gopls, JDT LS, Kotlin LSP, Ruby LSP, typescript-language-server, a project's own `tsc`, erb_lint, haml-lint and a project environment's Python tools. Their status reads "Off until you trust this folder".
- The first time one of them would start, a **Folder Trust** dialog asks once for that folder: **Stay Restricted** (the default, also Enter and Escape), **Trust** (Alt+T) or **Trust Parent Folder** (Alt+P). Trusting starts the held-back servers at once.
- The answer is remembered. A **Restricted** item in the status bar and the **Folder Trust…** command reopen the dialog, in the desktop and terminal apps. **Stop Trusting Project Tools in This Folder** returns a folder to Restricted.
- Syntax highlighting, search, Markdown, git views, Pyright and the HTML, CSS, YAML, shell and SQL tools work in Restricted folders. Pyright is not given a project's own interpreter path there.
- In every folder, project lookups (Gemfile, Haml, Cargo, go.work, TypeScript, pyrightconfig, Java and Kotlin builds) stop at the opened folder.
- A file opened without a folder gets these servers only when it is inside a trusted folder. Folders trusted in 0.0.18 stay trusted and now include their subfolders.

## Validation

The release commit passes the full local Linux gate and `scripts/perf-check.sh`. Lenz Code's terminal open benchmark shows no measurable change. Native macOS interaction (including Option+T), the fish shell and haml-lint after trusting remain unverified. Native package build/signature and CLI checks are separate from interactive validation. macOS packages are ad-hoc signed.

Keep all five executables together. Verify the matching `.sha256` sidecar before installation.

[Changes since 0.0.18](https://github.com/aantoniadis/lenz/compare/v0.0.18...v0.0.19).
